raw_plan.interpretation: One acquisition email for the selected audience, narrowed per the current dossier to freelancers delivering a client project. The email will invite an unknown-relationship reader to inspect Papier’s productivity planner rather than assume they use a particular tool or have experienced a specific planning failure.

intent.reason_now: A freelancer may be beginning a substantial client project that can be framed as a focused 16-week push.
intent.desired_action: Look inside the Your Plans on Paper productivity planner and judge whether its paper structure fits the project.

raw_plan.reader: A goal-driven freelancer considering a paper planning structure for a substantial client project over a focused 16-week period.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A goal-driven professional starting a focused 16-week push and wanting planning away from screens
raw_plan.reader_scope: Freelancers delivering a client project; do not generalise the product fit to every goal-driven professional.
raw_plan.promise: One client project can be given a defined 16-week place on paper, supported by goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.
raw_plan.orientation: A paper productivity planner for an individual freelancer organising daily work toward a substantial client project over a focused 16-week period.
raw_plan.arc: In one email, move the reader from recognising a relevant bounded planning format to inspecting the pages and deciding whether that structure suits their project.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: Because the audience is product-aware and only one email was requested, lead directly with the planner’s checkable 16-week mechanism and a read-only product-page action. Do not build the argument around the single-source rolling-calendar problem, since the planner only partially fits it and does not document a continuous view or linked notes.

emails.selection_reason: The 16-week undated format maps directly to the selected audience’s focused push, while goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily pages make the mechanism concrete enough to evaluate without relying on testimonials or promised results.
emails.target_audience: Freelancers delivering a client project within the selected goal-driven professional segment.
emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the planner and decide whether its 16-week paper structure fits one substantial client project.
emails.single_idea: Give one client project a defined 16-week place on paper, using undated pages, goal breakdowns and planning views at monthly, weekly and daily levels.
emails.felt_need: A substantial client project needs enough structure to connect the overall goal with the work that belongs on individual days.
emails.mechanism: The productivity planner provides 16 weeks of undated pages, supported by goal breakdowns, plus pages for monthly, weekly and daily planning. The reader can inspect that structure before deciding whether it fits the project.
emails.belief_shift: Before: a paper planner may seem like a general place for lists. After: this planner can be judged as a bounded 16-week structure for breaking down and planning one client project.
must_not_say: Do not claim the planner guarantees project completion, productivity gains, focus or goal achievement.
Do not claim it provides a continuous rolling calendar, a current-day-centred overview or links between notes and dates.
Do not imply integration or synchronisation with Obsidian, calendars, MS 365 or any other digital tool.
Do not state or imply that the recipient currently uses a particular app, printed calendar or task-management system.
Do not invent a deadline, missed milestone, prior failure, workload or pain for the recipient.
Do not generalise the fit beyond freelancers delivering a client project.
Do not use customer adoption, testimonials, comparative superiority or outcome proof; none is assigned to this argument.
Do not specify the structure or frequency of the goal breakdowns beyond the documented claim.
Do not add price, discounts, guarantees or delivery terms.
emails.tone: Artful, optimistic and purposeful, with crisp specificity rather than urgency.
emails.next_step_decision: Whether the planner’s 16-week, multi-timescale paper structure is suitable for organising one upcoming client project.
emails.next_step_value: The product page lets the reader inspect a planner documented as having 16 undated weeks, goal breakdowns and monthly, weekly and daily planning pages.
emails.next_step_limit: Looking inside does not establish a continuous rolling-date view, links to digital notes, compatibility with an existing workflow or any guaranteed project outcome.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the bounded 16-week client-project use case immediately recognisable; signal paper planning without inventing urgency, pain or a promised result.

raw_plan.voice_notes: Use Papier’s polished, lightly playful cadence, but keep the project-planning proposition concrete. Avoid productivity jargon and unsupported transformation language.

events.subject: Plan one client project on paper
events.preview_text: See how 16 undated weeks connect monthly, weekly and daily planning.
events.body:
Give one client project its own 16-week place on paper. Papier’s Your Plans on Paper Softback Spiral Productivity Planner offers an undated structure for mapping the work away from screens.

Begin with the goal breakdown, then use the monthly, weekly and daily planning pages to view the same project at different levels — from the wider shape to the work in front of you.

Because the 16 weeks are undated, the plan can begin with the project rather than a printed calendar date. One substantial piece of work, with a defined stretch of pages around it.

The product page lets you flick through the planner’s interior and inspect that structure before deciding whether it suits an upcoming client project.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Plan one project across 16 weeks"
events.subject: Plan one project across 16 weeks
events.preview_text: See how monthly, weekly and daily pages shape the work on paper.
events.body:
A substantial client project can take shape across **16 undated weeks**, on paper. Papier’s Your Plans on Paper Softback Spiral Productivity Planner gives it a clear beginning, middle and end.

Use the goal breakdowns to map the work, then move between monthly, weekly and daily planning pages as the project unfolds. The result is a bounded paper structure you can return to at each level—from the wider plan to the day in front of you.

The product page lets you flick through the planner and inspect those pages for yourself. See how the different planning views connect, then decide whether they suit one upcoming client project.

events.preview_text: Inspect the goal, monthly, weekly and daily page layouts before deciding.
events.body:
A client project can be planned at more than one scale: the wider shape, the week ahead and the next task on paper.

Papier’s Your Plans on Paper is a spiral-bound productivity planner with **16 undated weeks**, goal breakdowns and pages for monthly, weekly and daily planning.

The layouts are the important part. The question is whether their shapes and space suit the way you want to organise one client project—not whether they simply appear in the same planner.

On the product page, you can flick through the planner’s interior and compare the monthly, weekly and daily page layouts before deciding whether its 16-week structure belongs on your desk.
